searches.note: Twenty seven searches of a share of twenty eight, one left unspent, none of them the author's. Ten were restricted to a primary body's own domain and are read as primary through their summaries: doqpriorat.org twice, closmogador.com twice, masmartinet.com once, cellersdescaladei.com twice and patrimoni.gencat.cat once, with one restricted to four reference and press domains and one that blocked the importer's domain to find a second source. The shared two were the five clos of 1989 to 1991 and the DOQ's own dates of 2000 and 2009. No WebFetch was tried. Every record was tested; no fact that rests on no source was kept in a record marked checked.

method: Each record was read with one instruction, refute it: the founding year, the people and their dates, the classification, the grapes, the sites, the making and its months, the drinking window, the serving temperature, the label words, every beat of the story, the cards and the questions; then the house rules (nobody living named, no price, no score, nothing volatile, no judging superlative, no bare family word, British spelling, no dash).

The searches went first to the bodies' own pages (the DOQ, the houses, the Generalitat's heritage service) for their own dates, ranks and methods, then to the open web for the second source of each date and each story beat.

Where a search contradicted the record it was set right with its source (the Generalitat's year of 1990, the grape shares of Clos Mogador and Clos Erasmus, the ten clos names of 1989, the ageing of Clos Martinet); where a detail could be found in no source or the sources disagreed, it was cut or said with less (hand destemming at L'Ermita, stems at Clos Mogador, the naming of Laurel, the 500 litre barrels of Cartoixa, the share of carbonic maceration).

A fact that rests on one vintage's sheet was taken out of the making where the sources disagreed between vintages, and a question on one vintage's making was replaced by a question on the vineyard, which does not move with the year.
Sources whose title or address names a living person, or that are a writer's own site, were read in the results but never cited in the fragment or here.

tested: Founded 1989, the library's year and the year of the shared cellar: confirmed by the house's history in every account; Finca Dofí bought in 1990 in two accounts, so the record rightly gives it no year.

Gran Vinya Classificada, the first, from the 2017 vintage: the DOQ's own press pages (read through a search of doqpriorat.org) give L'Ermita as Gran Vinya Classificada from the 2017 vintage, later joined by two other wines by the end of 2020; Decanter and Wein.plus call it the first: confirmed.
The ladder presented in 2019: the DOQ's leaflet The Names of the Land is dated May 2019 by its own address; no decree was found: kept, with an open note.
The slope: north east facing, on slate, planted between 1900 and 1940 (Rare Wine Co, two merchants), below the hermitage of Our Lady of Consolation (Select Us Wines, Rare Wine Co): confirmed.

1993: the Rare Wine Co article says he found the slope in 1993, a merchant that he added it in 1993, and Decanter that he bought it shortly before the first vintage of 1993: the year confirmed, the verb set to acquired.

The founder's training: born into the Palacios Remondo family at Alfaro, studied oenology in Bordeaux and worked at Pétrus under the Moueix family (Grandi Bottiglie and two merchants): confirmed; the Moueix is not named, as the author ruled.
The invitation of the founder of Clos Mogador and the shared cellar of 1989 to 1991: two accounts: confirmed. Clos Dofí, from his nickname, the dolphin, became Finca Dofí: confirmed.

The making: about six weeks of maceration (42 and 44 days in the 2023 and 2024 sheets, 56 in the 2018), oak vats with the cap punched down, malolactic and ageing in French oak, oval foudres for the 2023 and 2024; hand destemming in one sheet only, part whole bunches in two: changed.
The blend: Garnacha with a little Cariñena and about 2 per cent white grapes in the 2017: confirmed.
Serve, ageing, glass and label: in the Codex's service reference for a full red; label terms the DOQ's own: sound.
The questions: one right answer each, distractors of one kind: sound. The house rules: no living person named but the house's own name, which the producer's name allows: sound.

changed.was: The bunches are destemmed by hand and the wine is macerated for about six weeks in oak vats, with the cap punched down. Malolactic fermentation and ageing follow in French oak, in the 2020s large oval foudres rather than new barrels, for a year to a year and a half before bottling.
changed.now: Fermented in oak vats with the cap punched down, after a long maceration of about six weeks. Malolactic fermentation and ageing follow in French oak for about a year to a year and a half before bottling; the cellar has moved from new barrels towards large oval foudres, used for the 2023 and the 2024.
changed.why: The sheets for 2023 and 2024 keep part of the fruit in whole bunches, so hand destemming is not the rule; one account gives new barrels for the 2022, so the foudres are dated to the vintages that show them.

tested: Founded 1979, the library's year: the house's own pages give the family's purchase of a few hectares of Garnacha near Gratallops in 1978 to 1979, the purchase of a building in 1986, the first vintage of 1989 and the first release of 1991: confirmed.

A family of French origin long in the Catalan wine trade: the house's family page gives the family's estate in the Vaucluse, the move to Tarragona after phylloxera and the bottling of Catalan wines by the founder's forebears: confirmed.

Vi de Finca Qualificada, the first in Spain: the house says so; Farr Vintners says the first in Spain, two accounts the first in Catalonia or in Priorat, by the Catalan authorities; the year is 2001, 2005, 2006 or 2008 by source: kept hedged as the house's, with no year.

The five clos and the shared cellar of 1989 to 1991, one pooled wine: confirmed by Wikipedia, Hudin, World of Fine Wine and two merchants; Wikipedia and Hudin add that the 1989 first went out under about ten clos names that settled into five: changed.
Clos as a word from Burgundy: in no source read: changed to the French word for an enclosed vineyard.
The blend: the house's 2010 sheet gives Garnacha 44, Cariñena 25, Syrah 16 and Cabernet Sauvignon 15 per cent: about half and nearly a third do not hold across vintages: changed.

The making: native yeasts alone and foudres of old wood on the house's pages, a year in 5,000 litre foudres in one place and eighteen months in 2,000 litre foudres in the author's sheets; stems in no page found: changed.
Manyetes, Nelin, the amphitheatre of llicorella: the house and the library: sound.

The questions: one right answer each; the second question's explanation leaned on 2009 as the year national law confirmed the DOQ, where the DOQ's own pages give the Catalan rank of 2000 and the state gazette's publication of its rules in 2009: changed.

changed.why: The house's 2010 sheet gives 44 and 25 per cent; shares that move with the year are not a typical blend.

changed.was: Fermented with native yeasts in large oak vats or open 300 litre barrels, part of the fruit with its stems, after a long maceration of four weeks and more. The house's sheets for 2020 and 2021 give about eighteen months in 2,000 litre foudres; those for 2017 and 2019 a mix of 300 litre casks and foudres.
changed.now: Fermented with native yeasts alone, in large oak vats or open 300 litre barrels, after a long maceration of four weeks and more. It is then aged in large old oak foudres, with smaller casks beside them in some years, for a year to a year and a half before bottling.
changed.why: A search of the house's domain found native yeasts alone and foudres of old wood, but nothing on stems; the cask sizes of four single vintages are the making of those vintages, not of the wine.

tested: Founded 1981: the house's History page, read through a search of masmartinet.com, gives the family's arrival and the estate's birth in 1981 and its first studies of slate, climate and the native vines; a retailer gives 1986: the house's year kept, hedged.

The handover: the house gives 2000 for the daughter taking control and credits her with the agroecological approach: around 2000 set to 2000, the olive groves and woods not in the page's summary: changed.

The site: the house places the plots of Mas d'en Martinet in the Gratallops wine area; the tourism board and the DOQ give the estate on the Falset road, in the municipality of Falset, but in the Gratallops wine area: confirmed.

The blend: the house lists Garnatxa, Carinyena, Garnatxa Peluda, Syrah, Merlot and Cabernet Sauvignon; a review gives 65 per cent Garnacha for the 2022; the author's 2021 listing gave Syrah the larger share: changed to in most years.

tested: The charterhouse: the Generalitat's heritage pages, read through a search of patrimoni.gencat.cat, give 1194 and Alfons el Cast, and the first Carthusian house of the Iberian Peninsula; the author's report gave 1163 for the Generalitat, which the refuter's search did not find; the twelfth century and no king stand either way: sound.
1835 and the confiscation of church lands: the heritage pages: confirmed.

The five families and their company of 1844, the Paris gold medal of 1878 (with Barcelona in 1888), the refounding of 1974: the house's own history page: confirmed; the label name Priorat de Scala-Dei is not the house's: changed.

The first Cartoixa of 1974 as the first Priorat bottled under the denomination's label: The Drinks Business, Spanish Wine Lover and Ara: confirmed and hedged; the house and Clos Mogador's family page claim earlier bottlings, left open.
The charterhouse given to the Generalitat: 1990 in a heritage page, a notarial agreement and the Diari de Tarragona, 1989 in a heritage guide, 1991 nowhere: changed.
Codorníu's entry in 2000: several accounts, with a stake of 25 per cent in most and control in one: the record says only that it bought in: sound.

The making and the sites: the house's Cartoixa page gives each lot fermented apart in small cement vats of 2,000 kilos, about three weeks on the skins and eighteen months of ageing, vineyards at 400 to 800 metres on clay terraces and slate slopes; no vessel for the ageing and no clay on the higher ground: changed.
The questions: one right answer each; the first's key now matches the house's words: sound.
